newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuraray to build synthetic fibre plant in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Kuraray to build synthetic fibre plant in Japan.

text.p: Kuraray Co Ltd said on Monday it would build a commercial plant for producing its new Kuraron K-II synthetic fibre as it expects growing demand for the product.
Kuraray said in a statement it would spend about five billion yen on building the plant, which will have a production capacity of 7,000 tonnes per year.
The plant, which will be located in the western prefecture of Okayama, is expected to start operating in April 1998.
Kuraray also plans to invest an additional 10 billion yen by the year 2000 to boost production to 25,000 tonnes, the statement said.
Sales of the new product are expected to reach about seven billion yen in the 1998/99 business year, and eventually grow to about 30 billion yen in the 2002/03 business year, the statement said.
Kuraray said the material is expected to have a wide range of applications in such areas as clothing, packaging, and electronic devices.
